What a /5 means

A /5 holds 134,217,728 addresses and is only seen as a large provider or registry aggregate.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /5 uses 5 network bits and leaves 27 host bits, so the block contains 134,217,728 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−5) − 2 = 134,217,728 − 2 = 134,217,726.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 0.0.0.1 248.0.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 0.0.0.0 7.255.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 0.0.0.1/5

Linux

ip addr add 0.0.0.1/5 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /5?

134,217,726. A /5 has 134,217,728 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 134,217,726 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /5?

248.0.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 7.255.255.255.
